name: Nursing Narrative Note Examples to Save Your License
seoTitle: Nursing Narrative Notes Book for RNs and LPNs
metaDescription: A charting guide full of narrative note examples for RNs and LPNs, a useful and budget friendly gift for new grads still finding words for tough moments.
summary: A charting guide with real narrative note examples, a budget friendly and thoughtful gift for new nurses who worry about documentation.
whyItWorks: Ask a new nurse what keeps them up after a shift, and charting comes up surprisingly often. Was that fall documented correctly? How do you describe a combative patient without sounding judgmental? Narrative notes are where nursing school examples run thin, and real situations rarely fit neatly into a template.

A book of narrative note examples gives a nurse words to borrow for the messy moments, from unusual behavior to family conflict to a patient refusing care. It is aimed at RNs and LPNs, so it suits both, and the focus on protecting your license speaks to a worry many new grads carry quietly. That makes it a smart gift for someone in their first year, a student close to graduation, or a nurse switching to a specialty with different charting expectations. It is budget friendly and small enough to keep in a work bag for quick reference on a slow night shift.
goodToKnow: Facility policies always come first, so the examples are guidance rather than rules.
It suits newer nurses most; veterans may already have their own phrasing.
Pair it with a nice pen or a pocket notebook.

faq.q: Is this a good gift for a new grad nurse?
faq.a: Yes, documentation is a common source of stress in the first year, and examples can build confidence.

faq.q: Can an LPN use this book?
faq.a: Yes, the title says it is written for both RNs and LPNs.
